title.narrative: Civic Education

description.narrative: Civic Education: Funding will support Civitas, a comprehensive civic education program that operates in both entities and whose goal is to help educate young Bosnians about the basic concepts of democratic society and to develop tolerance. This funding will support civic education during official pre-service teacher education in Bosnia and Herzegovina and will be used for designing and disseminating a system of continuous in-service teacher professional development in civic education. Special programming will be developed for home stay-based intercultural exchanges of students and teachers from different ethnic and religious backgrounds.

title.narrative: Civic Education

description.narrative: Civic Education: This funding will support a comprehensive civic education program that operates throughout the country and whose goal is to help educate young Bosnians about the basic concepts of democratic society, human rights, and tolerance. This funding will support civic education through the development of curricula, standards, and textbooks, as well as ongoing nationwide teacher education and in-service teacher professional development. Special programming will support homestay-based intercultural exchanges of students and teachers from different ethnic and religious backgrounds as well as interethnic cooperative projects in the field of civic education implemented through local school systems and other academic instituions.

title.narrative: Speakers Program

description.narrative: Speakers Program: This funding will support the engagement of recognized experts in a variety of policy-relevant fields for in-country consultations, lectures, seminars, training sessions, and workshops. These experts pass along practical skills, thereby creating a multiplier effect within the host country. The Speakers Program aims to provide a wide range of perspectives, promotes the recognition of fundamental liberties and individual freedoms, and increases civic participation. WithFY 2014 funds, visiting speakers will address variety of topics including, political participation of women, institutional capacity and strengthening of the Federation BIH Parliament Women Caucus, Euro-Atlantic integration, anti-corruption, human rights, rule of law, social media, and youth development.

title.narrative: Democracy Commission Small Grants Program

description.narrative: Democracy Commission Small Grants Program: The U.S. Embassys Democracy Commission gives small grants primarily to organizations engaged in building the social and intellectual foundations of democracy, supporting an independent media, the democratic resolution of problems, and the institutionalization of open, pluralistic political processes. Small grants are to be given for promotion of civil society; free flow of information (including support for independent media); transparency and accountability in government; public education, public advocacy campaigns that promote democratic practices and principles; association building; rule of law and legal reform; Euro-Atlantic integration; youth activism; conflict resolution; human rights; environment; market economy; anti-trafficking; anti-corruption awareness campaigns and training; ethnic and minority equality; and non-partisan election activities, such as get-out-the vote campaigns and monitoring. During FY 2014, Post introduced a new category of Continuation fund to support project proposals that have potential to build from previously successful projects with added elements that significantly contribute to more open and competitive political and economic systems and the protection of human rights.

title.narrative: Civic Education

description.narrative: Civic Education: Funding will support a comprehensive civic education program that operates in both entities and whose goal is to help educate young Bosnians about the basic concepts of democratic society, human rights and tolerance. This funding will support civic education during official pre-service teacher education nationwide and will be used for designing and disseminating a system of continuous in-service teacher professional development in civic education. Special programming will support homestay-based intercultural exchanges of students and teachers from different ethnic and religious backgrounds as well as interethnic cooperative projects in the field of civic education implemented through local school systems.
